This looks like a standard OIML certificate. The scheme field: "A" or "B". Hmm, the MAA (Mutual Acceptance Arrangement) came later. Certificates issued by NMIJ under R117 in 2016 — these are typically "basic" OIML certificates (not MAA). Actually the scheme A/B distinction relates to OIML-CS where scheme A is standard certificates and scheme B is MAA-based. Since this is 2016, likely scheme A (basic OIML Certificate system). The format "R117/1995-JP1-16.01" — JP1 indicates Japan as issuer number 1. I'll say scheme "A"... Actually, in the OIML-CS, certificates issued before MAA are considered scheme A. Let me think. The OIML-CS (Certificate System) started 2017, replacing the old "OIML Certificate System for Measuring Instruments". Before that, it was just "OIML certificates". The schema asks scheme (A|B). Given it's a standard certificate (not MAA), I'll put "A". Hmm, but I'm not fully sure. Actually, many extractors default to "A" for basic OIML certificates. I'll go with "A".

Wait — actually, let me reconsider. The OIML-CS defines: "OIML Certificates" issued under the Certificate System. Scheme A = traditional route (national issuer evaluates), Scheme B = MAA route (issued on basis of MAA evaluation). This 2016 certificate predates the MAA, so scheme "A" is reasonable.
